Hi all — quick technical response and attached redacted sample. Summary below; full details in the attached CSV (audit-sample-20260318.csv).

Key points:
- Schema: our standard audit export includes: timestamp_utc, request_id, hashed_user_id, action, resource_id, model_version, request_tokens, response_tokens, source_ip, region, actor_role (service_account/user), exported_at.
- Formats: exports available as CSV or JSON. Exports can be performed via the Audit Logs API (paginated JSON) or via the Console (CSV dump).
- Retention: Hosted (default) retention is 90 days. Dedicated customers can configure retention up to multi-year; Private deployments are customer-controlled and can meet 7+ years if backed by their storage policy. We can offer an export/archival pipeline to push logs to the customer's S3 for long-term retention (server-side encrypted).
- PII: we do not log raw PII fields by default. user identifiers in exports are hashed/opaque unless the customer requests a mapping and appropriate legal controls.
- Access controls: exports are gated by RBAC — only Ops/Platform roles and customer-authorized users can run exports. Every export is itself logged with an audit entry (who/when).
- Residency: for this account we can ensure log ingestion and export originate from US-only regions (must be scoped on the account and configured at provisioning time).

Deliverables attached: audit-sample-20260318.csv (redacted).

Next steps:
- If this looks good, propose a 30-minute technical deep-dive this week to walk through the API and show a live export.
- Marissa — please advise on any legal/privacy blockers to sharing the sample.

I can have a more detailed technical note (with sample API curl commands and export retention options) by EOD tomorrow if needed.

Thanks,
